resources.string: Do these steps in order, in the car, engine running. About 15 minutes. Everything is saved on the USB stick in a folder called cruise-fieldtest — bring the stick back to the computer afterwards.
Allow storage (to read the USB stick and save results), location (GPS speed while driving) and, if offered, ignore battery optimisation.
Records ignition off/on, sleep, USB stick, calls, navigation voice and steering keys. Leave it running while you drive for a few days; it saves to the USB stick by itself and stops after 3 days.
Reads the real Android version, chip, memory, screen, audio output and codecs.
Volume at a normal level. Play the left tone, then the right tone, then answer what you heard.
Shows a 6-second animation and then measures the processor for the sound engine. Do not touch the screen.

Start music in Cruise first (Folders). Then open Settings → Steering wheel: press every steering-wheel button (short, then long) and check each one shows up. Give the phone and sound-mixer buttons the jobs you want and try them. If you can, test answering and hanging up a call with the phone button. Then tap Done here.
Looks at the music on the USB stick: folders, formats, covers, read speed. Can take a few minutes for a big stick.
Copies the unit\'s audio and key settings and its built-in apps to the USB stick (up to 800 MB), so the steering wheel and ignition signals can be worked out on the computer.

With music playing in Cruise: 1) turn the ignition off, wait 1 minute, turn it on — the music should come back by itself. 2) Engage reverse for 5 seconds. 3) If you can: start a navigation voice instruction. Then tap Done.
Saves everything. Then: in the unit\'s Settings → About Device, tap \"Export locat.bin\". Photograph the steering-wheel, CAN and sound settings pages.
